newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican formal employment rises in April - Zedillo.
newsitem.headline: Mexican formal employment rises in April - Zedillo.

text.p: The number of permanent workers affiliated with the Mexican Social Security Institute increased by nearly 42,400 people during the second half of April, President Ernesto Zedillo said on Wednesday.

"The number of permanent workers affiliated with Social Security increased by almost 42,400 people, bringing the total figure for the year to 222,000," Zedillo said during a ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of the state housing institute Infonavit.
He gave no comparison to a previous fortnight.
The Social Security data are a broad indicator of employment in Mexico, reflecting the number of workers who will receive registered benefits as opposed to those working in the informal sector.

Zedillo said the figures "show that the effort that all of us are realizing has been worth it," referring to Mexico's painful recovery from the deep economic recession of 1995. ((-- Debora Montesinos, Mexico City newsroom, +525 728-7913))
